title: Human molecular imaging aging and SuperAging cohort
summary:
Our episodic memory enables us to remember personal experiences and events over the long term. As we age, our mental capacity and memory decline. However, the severity of this decline varies greatly between different people. A rapid decline in memory can also be an early sign of Alzheimer's disease, in which proteins are deposited in the brain, limiting the function of nerve cells. The aim of the central project Z03 is to better understand healthy cognitive ageing using different imaging techniques. To this end, a cohort of healthy, cognitively normal elderly (age ≥ 60 years) and "SuperAgers" will be established, who will be characterized for preclinical Alzheimer's pathology and other age-related patholgical changes (e.g. vascular disease). Cognitive abilities will be tested using neuropsychological tests, as well as blood analyses, medical and physical examinations, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and positron emission tomography (PET) scans in a proportion of the subjects. The study is the foundation of the Collaborative Research Centre 1436, in which the characterized age cohort will be further investigated in various subprojects. The aim is to understand which factors contribute to resilience or resistance to Alzheimer's pathology and age-related neurodegeneration.
The goal of the first funding period (2021–2024) is to establish the cohort (N~400) for the CRC. During the second funding period (2025–2028), longitudinal assessments will be conducted to capture trajectories of cognitive changes, brain  and biomarker alterations.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Written informed consent 
- Preserved legal capacity of the subjects at the respective time of the examination
- MRI suitability (not required if age >79)
- For PET: PET suitability
Exclusion criteria:
1. contraindications to MRI examinations: Pacemaker or defibrillator systems, tattoos, cochlear implants, insulin pumps, cerebral and ocular vascular clips or metal splinters, and marked claustrophobia, implants not suitable for MRI.
2. dementia syndromes
3. current severe neurological disease of the central nervous system (e.g. Parkinson's syndrome, motor neuron disease, temporal lobe epilepsy, multiple sclerosis)
4. current major depressive disorder and/or major neuropsychological disorder (schizophrenia, bipolar disorder)
5. current addiction (e.g. alcohol, psychological pharmaceuticals, cocaine, heroin) 
6. serious internal diseases (e.g. diabetes mellitus) 
7. Derailed vascular risk factors 
8. advanced renal and cardiac insufficiency
9. severe visual or hearing impairment (uncorrected) 
10. large tattoos
11. piercings
12. fear of confined spaces (claustrophobia)
13  contraindication for PET in young female participants: pregnancy
